theorem_title: Shao's Proposition 1.4: the weighted local result
natural_language_statement:
Let $m$ be an odd squarefree positive integer and let $f : \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z} \to [0,1]$ satisfy $\sum_{x \text{ unit}} f(x) > \frac{5}{8}\varphi(m)$. Then every $x$ modulo $m$ can be written $x = a_1 + a_2 + a_3$ with $a_1, a_2, a_3$ units, $f(a_1)f(a_2)f(a_3) > 0$ and $f(a_1) + f(a_2) + f(a_3) > \frac{3}{2}$.

The main theorem is the case $f = 1_A$ of this. The induction cannot be run on sets, because passing from $m$ to a prime factor splits $A$ into fibers of different densities, so the whole proof is carried by functions into $[0,1]$.

The constant $\frac{3}{2}$ is sharp. Take $m = 3$, $f(1) = 1$, $f(2) = \frac{1}{4}$ and $x = 2$, which forces the multiset $\{1, 2, 2\}$ and gives the sum exactly $\frac{3}{2}$.
source: Xuancheng Shao, "A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem", Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, arXiv:1206.6139v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139, Proposition 1.4
